With a straight‑line estimate of **≈ 780 miles**, most passenger cars won’t reach that far on a single tank.

#### Why Most Cars Won’t Make It Without Refueling

| Vehicle Type | Typical Fuel Tank Capacity* | Avg. Miles Per Gallon (MPG)** | Approx. Range |
|--------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------|---------------|
| Compact sedan | 12–14 gal | 30–35 mpg | 360–490 mi |
| Mid‑size SUV   | 18–20 gal | 22–28 mpg | 396–560 mi |
| Full‑size truck | 23–26 gal | 17–21 mpg | 391–546 mi |

\*Capacity varies by brand & trim.  
\*\*Average values – real numbers depend on load, terrain, weather, and maintenance.

Even under ideal conditions, none of those ranges come close to 780 mi. You’ll almost certainly need at least one stop for fuel (and possibly other services).

---

#### How to Verify Your Own Situation

If you’d like a precise “can I finish?” calculation:

1. **Know your vehicle’s specs**
   - *Make / Model*
